examples.text: We tried to hang the pictures so that the bottom of the frames were level with the dark line in the wallpaper.

examples.text: His pulse has been level for 12 hours.

 Are level now with men.

examples.text: The earth's oceans remain level in relation to the pull of gravity.

glosses: Degree or amount.

examples.text: This time was most dreadful for Lilian. Thrown on her own resources and almost penniless, she maintained herself and paid the rent of a wretched room near the hospital by working as a charwoman, sempstress, anything. In a moment she had dropped to the level of a casual labourer.

glosses: Achievement or qualification.

examples.text: She achieved a high level of distinction.

glosses: Distance from the root node of a tree structure.

examples.text: Many of the levels change over time, from day to night or from one location to another, and some undergo a total transformation.

glosses: A numeric value given to a character (or other element of a game) that represents its relative power, challenge or eligibility to do things, used as a game mechanic to govern progression through a game.

examples.text: My half-orc barbarian reached fifth level before he was squashed by a troll.

glosses: A floor of a multi-storey building.

examples.text: Take the elevator and get off at the promenade level.

glosses: An area of almost perfectly flat land.

examples.text:

examples.text: The most common level of the colour variable is red. The other levels are blue and green.

examples.text: You can level the table by turning the pads that screw into the feet.

glosses: To destroy by reducing to ground level; to raze.

examples.text: The hurricane leveled the forest.

glosses: To progress to the next level.

examples.text: I levelled after defeating the dragon.

glosses: To aim or direct (a weapon, a stare, an accusation, etc).

examples.text: He levelled an accusation of fraud at the directors.  The hunter levels the gun before taking a shot.

examples.text: If the right of killing salmon belong exclusively to the King, and consequently to his donatories, why has not the Legislature secured the right by levelling penalties against such as should encroach upon it … ?

glosses: To make the score of a game equal.

examples.text: Holt was furious referee Michael Oliver refused to then award him a penalty after Ledley King appeared to pull his shirt and his anger was compounded when Spurs immediately levelled.
